title: A refined valuative criterion with a dense subscheme implies universal closedness, and separatedness when the morphism is quasi-separated
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a refined valuative criterion: if a quasi-compact morphism has a quasi-compact dense subscheme through which every valuation ring diagram admits a unique filler, then the morphism is universally closed, and separated as well when it is quasi-separated (statement lines 10219-10234). The counted proof is long and technically dense: it reduces to reduced schemes and an affine base, passes to a flat polynomial algebra cover so that the base changed dense open has the whole spectrum as scheme theoretic image, applies the existence statement for valuation diagrams to produce an auxiliary valuation ring, then invokes the existence of a dominating valuation ring inside a residue field and a sandwich construction to put the situation into the shape required by the hypothesis, and finally pulls the dotted arrow back to the original valuation ring by maximality for the domination order (proof lines 10236-10302); the separatedness half is deduced by running the same argument for the quasi-compact diagonal (proof lines 10304-10327). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with several genuinely distinct reduction steps, and the cited inputs are standard criteria and algebra facts.
